thread:
sam_sales: Quick Q from a POC — customer has SD-WAN into a TGW (active/active) and wants to reach our PrivateLink connector. They need a regional fallback to an outbound proxy if the PrivateLink path is unavailable, and they want to preserve client source IP for auth logs. Also asking for cost tradeoffs (Hosted vs Dedicated). Any recommended topology or known blockers?

maria_solutions: TL;DR: interface endpoint + NLB in our VPC is simplest. Source IP preservation depends on whether traffic hits a NAT/proxy. If they need the original client IP inside our backend, avoid SNAT (so NLB -> instances without NAT). If TLS inspect happens at their edge that will rewrite/terminate TLS unless they use XFF from a proxy. :thinking_face:

raj_netops: A few clarifying Qs before we recommend: 1) SD-WAN -> TGW (spoke) — is it a transit TGW or do they terminate into a spoke only? 2) How do they plan route failover (BGP vs static)? 3) Will they perform TLS inspect at corporate perimeter or just at proxy?

alex_customer: They terminate into a spoke attached to TGW. Expect active/active. TLS inspect is on their corporate perimeter before it hits the spoke. We want to avoid double NAT if possible.

maria_solutions: Given that: option A (recommended for simplest security model): create an interface endpoint (PrivateLink) backed by a TCP NLB in our service VPC, NLB targets our connector instances. Make sure NLB mode preserves client IP (TCP NLB preserves IP to target). Route table in the spoke needs a route to the endpoint ENI (use the endpoint's prefix list id). For fallback: use a policy route or BGP path-preference to steer to an outbound proxy ENI when the endpoint is unreachable.

maria_solutions: Example AWS CLI route create (illustrative):
```
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc1234 --destination-prefix-list-id pl-0abcd1234 --network-interface-id eni-0a1b2c3d4e
```
(we'll provide exact commands once we know their RTB IDs)

raj_netops: Important on src IP: if traffic goes through a NAT gateway or NAT instance it will be SNATed and you lose client IP. To keep client IP: 1) use NLB -> instance targets so src IP is preserved, 2) ensure security groups accept the customer's source CIDRs (PrivateLink will show endpoint ENIs as source), and 3) avoid adding NAT in front of the connector. If TLS inspect sits in customer's path, that device will terminate TLS and re-initiate a TLS session — the caller IP will still be the original client IP but the cert will be theirs; we need to validate mutual TLS or token auth accordingly.

maria_solutions: Cost/ops notes: interface endpoints have hourly ENI costs + data processing per GB. NLB has hourly + LB data processing. Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) often reduces per-token inference cost for steady traffic — but adds fixed monthly commitment. Hosted is simpler (no infra setup) but can have higher variable cost and you can't control private VPC peering. Adding an outbound proxy implies additional egress charges on their account and possible additional egress in our dedicated infra if we host a proxy. We'll run a basic cost sketch for the POC.

sam_sales: Action items: raj_netops to write a short runbook for route flip/failover and a minimal healthcheck for automation; maria_solutions to estimate endpoint+NLB+egress cost for a 1TB/month baseline; I'll send a diagram to the customer and confirm whether they can avoid TLS inspect for this path. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Ticket IDS-4231 created: "privatelink-fallback-proxy-poc" assigned to raj_netops,maria_solutions — link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/IDS-4231

alex_customer: Thanks — one more ask: what exact firewall ports do we need to open on their side (spoke/TGW + outbound proxy)?

maria_solutions: Minimal firewall checklist:
- Outbound TCP 443 to the NLB's listener IPs (or DNS name)
- If using health checks, allow TCP from NLB health-check IP ranges to the connector health port (we'll publish exact SGs)
- If they put a proxy in the path, allow 443 to the proxy ENI and allow the proxy to talk to the NLB on 443
- For management/metrics, allow outbound to our telemetry endpoints (we'll provide FQDNs)

raj_netops: MTU/SD-WAN gotcha: SD-WAN overlays can reduce path MTU. Recommend enabling TCP MSS clamping on their edge so upstream can't send large MSS that will cause fragmentation. Example iptables rule for an AWS transit instance / edge box (illustrative):
```
iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
This prevents weird TLS handshake issues when MTU is low.

sam_sales: Great. mari/raj — can you drop the runbook and cost sketch in the ticket by EOD tomorrow? I'll follow up with the customer after that.

alex_customer: Appreciated, looking forward to the diagram and runbook.
